title: Akvan's northward shift brings heavy to very heavy rain forecast for the Midnapores on Friday
dek: Kolkata's weather office forecasts 7-20 cm at isolated places in East and West Midnapore and asks fishermen to stay off the Bengal coast on Thursday and Friday, as the IMD moves the cyclone's landfall north to between Narsapur and Puri.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Heavy to very heavy rain of 7-20 cm is very likely at one or two places in East and West Midnapore on Friday, 20 November, as Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan crosses the coast to the south-west, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Kolkata said in its 4 pm special bulletin on Wednesday, raising its earlier forecast of heavy rain for the two districts. Heavy rain of 7-11 cm is likely at one or two places in North and South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore and Jhargram on Thursday, and in South 24 Parganas, Jhargram, Bankura and Howrah on Friday.

The change follows the India Meteorological Department's (IMD) decision on Wednesday to move the storm's expected landfall north, to the stretch between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha, around noon on Friday. The IMD now forecasts that the weakening storm will move north over Odisha towards Jharkhand on Friday night and Saturday, and that Gangetic West Bengal will get heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places on Friday. The RMC has now also asked fishermen not to go out along and off the West Bengal coast on 19 and 20 November. Distant Warning Signal No. 2 remains hoisted at the Kolkata and Haldia docks.

## Latest forecast

According to the RMC's Wednesday bulletin, light to moderate rain is likely at a few places in North and South 24 Parganas, the two Midnapores, Jhargram, Kolkata and Howrah until Thursday morning. On Thursday rain becomes very likely at many places in those districts and in Hooghly, with heavy falls in the coastal and near-coastal districts, and thunderstorms with gusts of 40-50 kmph at one or two places in South 24 Parganas and East Midnapore. On Friday rain is very likely at most places in Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly, Bankura and the southern districts, with the heaviest falls in the two Midnapores. On Saturday heavy rain is likely at one or two places in Purulia as the storm's remnants move inland, and showers are forecast across south Bengal until Monday, with dry weather from 24 November.

The RMC warned of lightning strikes, especially in open fields, temporary waterlogging in low-lying areas and underpasses on 19 and 20 November, some damage to standing crops and horticulture, and damage to vulnerable kutcha houses, including the possibility of walls collapsing. It advised people not to shelter under trees or electric poles, to avoid kutcha houses, to keep harvested paddy in a safe place, and said beach and recreational activities and traffic should be regulated on 19 and 20 November. North Bengal is expected to stay largely dry, with light rain at one or two places in Malda and the two Dinajpurs from Friday.

Fishermen have been told not to go into the deep sea of the northwest and westcentral Bay of Bengal until 20 November, and not to go out along and off the West Bengal coast on 19 and 20 November; those already at sea have been asked to return, the RMC said. Squally winds of 40-50 kmph gusting to 60 kmph are expected along the Bengal coast on both days, with rough seas. Over the northwest Bay, winds are expected to strengthen to gale force, 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph, from Thursday morning until Friday noon, with very rough to high seas.

In its 6.10 pm national bulletin on Wednesday, the IMD said the storm lay about 660 km south of Gopalpur and 720 km south of Puri at 2.30 pm and was moving north-north-west at 8 kmph. It forecast gale winds of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph along and off the north Odisha and West Bengal coasts from Thursday morning to Friday noon.

## For the fishing fleets

The forecast winds and rough seas over the northwest Bay, and the new ban on fishing off the Bengal coast, matter for the trawler fleets of Digha, Kakdwip, Namkhana and Frasergunj, which work these waters.

## Why it matters for Bengal

Rain in the second half of November comes as the aman paddy crop, south Bengal's main rice crop, approaches harvest, and as potato planting begins in districts such as Hooghly and Paschim Medinipur; heavy rain at this stage can flatten ripe paddy and waterlog fields. Bengal escaped the worst of Cyclone Arnab and Cyclone Murasu, which hit Andhra Pradesh and Odisha in late October and early November.

## What happens next

The RMC in Kolkata updates its special bulletins as the storm moves, and the IMD issues national bulletins every three hours; its next was due at 9 pm on Wednesday. The state government had not announced any special measures for the storm by Wednesday evening. The Declaration will update this story as forecasts for Bengal are revised.
